answers.question: Is the property currently compliant for gas safety?
answers.answer: Yes, today. The compliance record shows a CP12 issued 2025-10-17 and expiring 2026-10-16 (Gas Safe 550123, which matches HeatRight). I trust it over the legacy note ('renewed 2025, all good'), which is vague, unsigned and from the old agency. It is only compliant until 16 Oct; the certificate itself wasn't seen.

answers.question: What steps do you take to get access lawfully before expiry?
answers.answer: Sent written notice to the tenant asking for times and saying 24h written notice will follow once a time is fixed. Earlier email and SMS went unanswered. Next, on 12 Oct: phone call, then posted/hand-delivered letter, then escalate to compliance. No forced entry; holding keys gives no right of entry.

answers.question: What do you tell the landlord?
answers.answer: Ben has been told the certificate expires 16 Oct, the tenant hasn't responded, and has been asked to approve HeatRight Ltd (preferred contractor, cost not yet known, limit £300) or arrange his own.

This is written notice that we are arranging a Gas Safe engineer (HeatRight Ltd) to visit. Please reply with days and times that suit you in the next few days, or call us. If you ever smell gas, leave the property, don't use switches or flames, and call 0800 111 999. Thank you.
